name: Miconazole/hydrocortisone (topical)
className: Imidazole antifungal with mild topical corticosteroid

formulations.label: Cream
formulations.note: The only UK SmPC found for this combination is a pharmacy-sale (P) pack: maximum 7 days, and section 4.3 limits some uses (children under 10, ano-genital area, ringworm, secondary infection) to doctor prescription. Contains benzoic acid and butylhydroxyanisole (local irritation).

src.q: Miconazole nitrate 2% w/w; Hydrocortisone acetate equivalent to hydrocortisone 1% w/w.
The maximum period of treatment is 7 days.
Children under 10 years of age, unless prescribed by a doctor
This medicine contains 2 mg/g of Benzoic acid (E210) which may cause local irritation.
Butylhydroxyanisole (E320) which may cause local skin reactions

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Athlete's foot and candidal intertrigo with co-existing inflammation (initial stage of treatment; continue with a miconazole-only product once inflammation settles).

src.q: Athlete's foot and candidal intertrigo where there are co-existing symptoms of inflammation.
indicate it particularly for the initial stages of treatment

items.t: UK pack is a pharmacy-sale product: section 4.3 says not for children under 10 years, the ano-genital region, ringworm or secondarily infected conditions unless prescribed by a doctor.

src.q: Children under 10 years of age, unless prescribed by a doctor
On the ano-genital region unless prescribed by a doctor To treat ringworm unless prescribed by a doctor To treat secondary infected conditions unless prescribed by a doctor

items.t: Apply twice a day to the affected area and rub in gently until absorbed. Maximum treatment period 7 days.

src.q: Apply the cream twice a day to the affected area, rubbing in gently until the cream has been absorbed by the skin.
The maximum period of treatment is 7 days.

items.t: Elderly: skin is naturally thinner, so use sparingly and for short periods.

src.q: Natural thinning of the skin occurs in the elderly, hence corticosteroids should be used sparingly and for short periods of time.

items.t: Section 4.3: not for children under 10 years unless prescribed by a doctor. Clinical trials included children from 1 month to 14 years; irritability was common (3.2%) in one infant napkin-dermatitis trial.

src.q: Children under 10 years of age, unless prescribed by a doctor
The frequency of irritability in Daktacort Hydrocortisone Cream-treated paediatric patients was common (3.2%).

items.t: Use with caution under occlusion, including nappies.

src.q: caution is advised when Daktacort Hydrocortisone Cream is to be applied to extensive surface areas or under occlusive dressings including baby napkins

items.t: Hypersensitivity to miconazole or other imidazoles, hydrocortisone or any excipient.

src.q: Known hypersensitivity to miconazole or other imidazole derivatives, hydrocortisone or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Tubercular or viral skin infections, or skin infections caused by Gram-negative bacteria.

src.q: Tubercular or viral infections of the skin or those caused by Gram-negative bacteria.

items.t: Should not be used on broken skin, on large areas, for longer than 7 days, for cold sores or acne, or on the face, eyes or mucous membranes.

src.q: If the skin is broken On large areas of skin Used for longer than 7 days To treat cold sores and acne Use on the face, eyes and mucous membranes

items.t: Unless prescribed by a doctor: children under 10 years, the ano-genital region, ringworm, secondarily infected conditions.

src.q: Children under 10 years of age, unless prescribed by a doctor

items.t: Warfarin or other vitamin K antagonists: miconazole inhibits CYP3A4/2C9; use with caution and carefully monitor and titrate the anticoagulant effect.

src.q: the concomitant use of Daktacort Hydrocortisone Cream and warfarin or other vitamin K antagonists should be done with caution and the anticoagulant effect should be carefully monitored and titrated

items.t: Severe hypersensitivity (including anaphylaxis and angioedema) has been reported; stop if hypersensitivity or irritation occurs.

src.q: Severe hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and angioedema, have been reported
If a reaction suggesting hypersensitivity or irritation should occur, the treatment should be discontinued.

items.t: Must not contact the eye mucosa. Avoid application to the face; caution on extensive areas or under occlusion (including nappies). Avoid long-term continuous use: adrenal suppression can occur even without occlusion.

src.q: Daktacort Hydrocortisone Cream must not come into contact with the mucosa of the eyes.
similarly application to the face should be avoided
Long term continuous topical corticosteroid therapy should be avoided. Adrenal suppression can occur even without occlusion.

items.t: Blurred vision or other visual disturbance: consider referral to an ophthalmologist.

src.q: the patient should be considered for referral to an ophthalmologist for evaluation of possible causes

items.t: May damage latex contraceptives (condoms, diaphragms) and some synthetic fabrics; avoid contact and wear cotton underwear over treated areas.

src.q: Contact should be avoided between latex products such as contraceptive diaphragms or condoms and Daktacort Hydrocortisone Cream since the constituents of Daktacort Hydrocortisone Cream may damage the latex.
it is recommended to wear cotton underwear if this clothing comes into contact with the affected area

items.t: Topical steroid withdrawal reactions can follow long-term or inappropriate use of topical corticosteroids (MHRA).

src.q: long-term continuous or inappropriate use of topical corticosteroids, particularly those of moderate to high potency, can result in the development of rebound flares after stopping treatment

items.t: Warfarin and other vitamin K antagonists: miconazole (CYP2C9 inhibition) can increase the anticoagulant effect, even from topical products. Use with caution, monitor INR and reduce the warfarin dose if needed; the patient should stop the cream and seek advice if bleeding signs occur.

src.q: in patients on warfarin or other vitamin K antagonists, caution should be exercised and anticoagulant effect should be monitored
if miconazole and warfarin are used concurrently, the anticoagulant effect should be carefully monitored and, if necessary, the dose of warfarin reduced
Patients should be advised of the symptoms of bleeding events and to immediately stop treatment with miconazole and seek medical advice should they occur

items.t: Miconazole inhibits CYP3A4 and can slow hydrocortisone metabolism: serum hydrocortisone may be higher than with hydrocortisone-only cream.

src.q: Serum concentrations of hydrocortisone may be higher with the use of Daktacort Hydrocortisone Cream compared with topical preparations containing hydrocortisone alone.

renal.note: The UK SmPC gives no renal advice.

hepatic.note: The UK SmPC gives no hepatic advice.

items.t: SmPC: limited data; corticosteroids cross the placenta. As a precaution, preferably avoid in pregnancy; avoid large areas and occlusive dressings.

src.q: As a precautionary measure, it is preferable to avoid the use of Daktacort Hydrocortisone during pregnancy.
Treatment of large surfaces and the application under occlusive dressing should be avoided during that time.

items.t: BUMPS: topical corticosteroids (hydrocortisone is named) can be used in pregnancy. No BUMPS leaflet for topical miconazole was found.

src.q: Topical corticosteroids can be used in pregnancy.

items.t: SmPC: caution during breastfeeding; avoid large areas and occlusive dressings; a risk to the newborn cannot be excluded.

src.q: Caution is recommended during breast-feeding.
A risk to the newborn child cannot be excluded.

items.t: SPS: topical hydrocortisone can be used during breastfeeding, with no extra risk from combination products containing antimicrobials. No SPS page for topical miconazole was found.

src.q: When applied to the skin, used rectally or for use in the ear, hydrocortisone can be used during breastfeeding.
There are no additional risks when combination topical preparations containing antimicrobials or urea are used.

reproductive.note: The UK SmPC has no fertility statement. Latex contraceptives may be damaged (see cautions).

items.t: No adverse reactions occurred in 1% or more of trial patients. Uncommon: skin irritation, skin burning. Irritability was common (3.2%) in infants with napkin dermatitis in one trial.

src.q: No adverse drug reactions (ADRs) were reported by ≥ 1% of the 480 Daktacort Hydrocortisone Cream-treated patients
The frequency of irritability in Daktacort Hydrocortisone Cream-treated paediatric patients was common (3.2%).

items.t: Anaphylaxis, angioedema and other severe hypersensitivity: stop treatment.

src.q: Severe hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and angioedema, have been reported
If a reaction suggesting hypersensitivity or irritation should occur, the treatment should be discontinued.

items.t: Bleeding (bruising, nosebleeds, blood in urine) in patients taking warfarin: stop the cream and seek medical advice.

src.q: seek medical advice if they notice signs of over-anticoagulation during treatment, such as sudden unexplained bruising, nosebleeds or blood in the urine
Patients should be advised of the symptoms of bleeding events and to immediately stop treatment with miconazole and seek medical advice should they occur

items.t: Topically applied corticosteroids can be absorbed enough to cause systemic effects with prolonged, excessive use.

src.q: Topically applied corticosteroids can be absorbed in sufficient amounts to produce systemic effects.

items.t: Patients on warfarin or another vitamin K antagonist: monitor the anticoagulant effect (INR) carefully and titrate.

src.q: When Daktacort Hydrocortisone Cream is used by patients taking oral anticoagulants, the anticoagulant effect should be carefully monitored.

items.t: Stop if hypersensitivity or irritation occurs; do not use for more than 7 days.

src.q: If a reaction suggesting hypersensitivity or irritation should occur, the treatment should be discontinued.
The maximum period of treatment is 7 days.

items.t: For use on the skin only. Rub in gently until absorbed; keep away from the eyes.

src.q: rubbing in gently until the cream has been absorbed by the skin
Daktacort Hydrocortisone Cream must not come into contact with the mucosa of the eyes.

items.t: Tell the doctor or pharmacist if taking warfarin before using any miconazole product; report unexplained bruising, nosebleeds or blood in the urine.

src.q: Patients should be advised to tell their doctor or pharmacist if they are receiving warfarin before using products that contain miconazole

items.t: Can damage condoms and diaphragms; wear cotton underwear over treated areas.

src.q: Once the inflammatory conditions have disappeared treatment may be continued with Daktarin Cream or Daktarin powder

rules.concern: Hypersensitivity to miconazole, other imidazoles or hydrocortisone
rules.consequence: Hypersensitivity reaction; severe reactions including anaphylaxis and angioedema have been reported with this cream and other topical miconazole products.

src.q: Known hypersensitivity to miconazole or other imidazole derivatives, hydrocortisone or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

rules.concern: Topical miconazole with warfarin (or another vitamin K antagonist)
rules.consequence: Miconazole inhibits CYP3A4/2C9 and can prolong the effect of warfarin or other vitamin K antagonists; systemic absorption from the skin is limited, but MHRA warns that miconazole, including topical forms, can enhance the anticoagulant effect.
rules.action: Use with caution; carefully monitor INR and titrate (reduce warfarin dose if needed). Patient to stop the cream and seek advice if bleeding occurs.
rules.sourceWording: should be done with caution and the anticoagulant effect should be carefully monitored and titrated

src.q: the concomitant use of Daktacort Hydrocortisone Cream and warfarin or other vitamin K antagonists should be done with caution and the anticoagulant effect should be carefully monitored and titrated
Miconazole administered systemically is known to inhibit CYP3A4/2C9, which can lead to prolonged effects of warfarin or other vitamin K antagonists.
Miconazole, including the topical gel formulation, can enhance the anticoagulant effect of warfarin
if miconazole and warfarin are used concurrently, the anticoagulant effect should be carefully monitored and, if necessary, the dose of warfarin reduced

src.q: As a precautionary measure, it is preferable to avoid the use of Daktacort Hydrocortisone during pregnancy.

Administration of corticosteroids to pregnant animals can cause abnormalities of foetal development.
Treatment of large surfaces and the application under occlusive dressing should be avoided during that time.
